meta_description: Portland's Heritage Trees, the trunkless Octopus Tree at Cape Meares and a burning Douglas fir that lived. {trees} Oregon trees across {places} places.
intro: Oregon's giants grow in two very different places. On the coast stand the conifers the loggers missed: the Doerner Fir in the Coos Bay backcountry, which survived a fire in its own crown in 2025, and the Octopus Tree at Cape Meares, a Sitka spruce with no trunk at all, only limbs rising from the ground like a candelabra. In Portland the old trees are street trees, and the city keeps a Heritage Tree list that protects them one address at a time: an elm an architect once blocked with his own car, a pine a florist planted before there was a street, a sequoia forty-five metres tall on a residential verge.
